test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If an object is placed 36 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 18 cm, then its image will be formed __________.

options.text: at 36 cm in front of the mirror
at 18 cm in front of the mirror

solution:
The correct answer is __**at 36 cm in front of the mirror**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The focal length (f) of the concave mirror is given as 18 cm.
 
• The object distance (u) is given as -36 cm (negative as per sign convention).
 
• Using the mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u.
 
• Substituting the known values: 1/18 = 1/v - 1/36, solving this gives v = -36 cm (negative sign indicates that the image is formed in front of the mirror).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror that has a reflecting surface that bulges inward.
 
• It converges light to a point in front of the mirror, which is why it is also called a converging mirror.
 
• It is used in applications where focusing light is necessary, such as in telescopes, vehicle headlights, and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula:**
 
 
• The mirror formula is given by the equation: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance.
 
• According to the sign convention, all distances are measured from the pole of the mirror. Distances measured in the direction of the incident light are taken as positive, and those measured against the direction of the incident light are taken as negative.
 
• This formula is essential in determining the position and nature (real or virtual) of the image formed by spherical mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention:**
 
 
• For mirrors, the object distance (u) is always negative since the object is placed in front of the mirror.
 
• The focal length (f) is negative for concave mirrors and positive for convex mirrors.
 
• The image distance (v) is positive if the image is formed behind the mirror (virtual image) and negative if the image is formed in front of the mirror (real image).
 
 
 
• **Image Formation by Concave Mirror:**
 
 
• If the object is placed at the center of curvature (C), the image is formed at C, is real, inverted, and of the same size as the object.
 
• If the object is placed between the center of curvature (C) and the focal point (F), the image is formed beyond C, is real, inverted, and larger than the object.
 
• If the object is placed beyond the center of curvature (C), the image is formed between C and F, is real, inverted, and smaller than the object.
